title: Disappointing Thick Lead
review: I have a thick slip lead which I have been pleased with and recommended to others and I went on to buy the thick clip lead and was disappointed to find it was not as thick and comfortable to hold, or on the dog, as the slip lead. On discussion with customer services, who were prompt in their reply, I understand this was due to a fault at the factory which means it is thinner but stronger.  Firstly, I didn't know the original was weak and needed to be made stronger, and secondly, if they know there is a fault but still sell it as advertised, well I don't think that's trustworthy.  It's a shame because I have used and recommended Rough & Tumble for leads and dog coats and I'm not sure I will again as I can't be sure that what I will receive is what they are advertising.Thank you for your reply, to clarify the reply that I received following my initial enquiry,  I have copied and pasted the reply below (I've anonymised the sender):Hi Car​o,​Thanks so much for your email.​I've asked our director and this was accidentally done by our factory - but with the weave being tighter so the Lead is slightly thinner, it does make for a stronger Lead!​Kind regards,MCCustomer Services03332 079960email removedWebsite removed

description:
A truly tailored solution to parasite protection

Our goal is simple: to keep every pet protected from parasites, by making parasite protection as easy and accessible as possible.

We deliver flea, tick and worm treatments through your letterbox in exactly the right doses for your pet, at exactly the right time. Simply answer a few questions about your pet, and select from a range of treatment options. We’ll tailor their treatments and put everything in their very own personalised dispensing envelope. When it arrives in the post, it’s time to dose! You’ll never forget to protect, and you can enjoy the convenience of having your pet’s care on your doormat when you need it.

Vet-recommended treatments you can trust

Our protection options include the UK’s No. 1 flea treatment, Frontline Plus, as well as market-leaders, Drontal and Dronspot, and other reputable products that are safe, effective and provide long-lasting protection. As a team of veterinary professionals ourselves, we wouldn’t have it any other way.

A commitment-free subscription that you control

Everything you need to manage your subscription is available at your fingertips via your online account. Make changes to your pet’s protection, add other pets to your subscription, pause or cancel deliveries and more.

Want to know more?

review: I am disabled (hidden severe, crumbling, spinal) prior to our delivery, in the notes (or add info section) I ensured that I’d noted that to please if poss to give me prior warning, as it takes me time to get to the my front door. I have had prev unpleasant experiences with the delivery person, who was going to just leave our 27kg box on the front steps - I hd hoped they hd been resolved, we do not have a closed in porch. I asked to pls just push into our hall - he snapped ´I have a hernià’- i sympathised & then embarrassingly hd to tell him, that I live with a crumbling spine, titanium top & bottom of my spine. Only, after I asked for his name, did he most begrudgingly put the box at the v front of our hall. To which I thanked him profusely & wished him a good recovery.  I have prev left notes on our front door stating the same. This time he waited no time for me to even get to the front door. They just left the large box in full view, in front of our car , no cover or protection.  At mid day - it had to wait until my husband came home from work in the evening. Absolutely no consideration for the fact I’m disabled. What would happen if it had been stolen ?? It’s our darling boys kibble & not cheap. It was really v stressful & quite unnecessary experience. A v sorry state of affairs 😞Your staff at Angell pet Co are terrific, thank you to them all. We hope you all have a wonderful Christmas & New year. Best wishes to you all 😍

title: They don't produce their own dog food
review: I'm really disappointed in Ci Food. I've only recently found out that they don't produce their own dog food, they just buy it from a bigger company, put their own label on the package and sell it to us as if they have produced it themselves. If you don't believe me, you can copy the ingredients of whatever Ci Food you're feeding your dog and paste it to Google. Then you will see that the exact same kibble / wet food with the exact same recipe is sold by other brands as well. For example, I was feeding my dog Tickety Boo Large Breed Puppy (Salmon, Sweet Potato & Vegetables) and Top Drawer Puppy Chicken & Rice. If you copy the ingredients of Tickety Boo Large Breed Puppy and paste it to Google, you will see that the exact same kibble with the exact same recipe is also sold under different names by brands like Furlington, Country Kibble, Challenge Dog Food, Dog's Life Dog Food, Canine Kitchen, Luv Dogz, etc. etc. - brands I've never even heard of before. And the list goes on. Obviously they all buy the same kibble from the same big company, put their own labels and prices on it, and sell it as if they've produced it themselves. Similarly when I've copied and pasted the ingredients of Top Drawer Puppy Chicken & Rice, again I've seen that the exact same wet food with the exact same recipe is also sold under different names by brands like Pets Love Europa, PawPrints, Lovejoys, etc. I recommend you google the ingredients of whatever you are feeding your dog as well. When these companies tell us things like 'we have developed this recipe' or 'we have added this and that to this kibble', they are lying to us because they have never produced the kibble themselves in the first place. They simply buy and sell it and only care about the profit they make.

It has not flavour by the smell, just smells really sweet. My boy is fussy with feeds, hay, treats and supplements but he absolutely loves this. His been in this since summer last year and his been very happy on it so I definitely can give it a 5 star. I also use their linseed meal and turmeric extra and has been amazing! Used them for almost a year also and have had no problems. Absolutely love their products and will continue to use them in the future

title: Great as a free service, but don't pay
review: Great as a free service, but don't bother paying.I used their free service to get a vet nurse appointment about our dog's itchy skin. She recommended some products to buy, we bought one that didn't really work. Later on, I used it again to get an actual vet appointment through our insurance which was offered by Waggel for free. However, the vet offered near enough the exact same recommendations as the vet nurse. Had I paid for  this, I'd be annoyed.Never pay for an appointment with them. Only ever  use the free vet nurse appointments, or free through your insurance. They cannot provide prescriptions and so their advice only ever extends to being just advice about over the counter products you can buy, or recommending you to go to an actual high street vet. £30 for a vet appointment when an actual high street vet appointment is £30-£50, it doesn't make sense to waste your time and money.

title: I was a little unsure about booking…
review: I was a little unsure about booking with Behavet as my first instinct of the website and sales call was a lot  about how the services are 'free' if you have insurance with certain companies. It felt a little like that was the main 'selling point' of the consultations, however it was recommended by a friend so I signed up. I wish I had gone with my gut. Although the vet was very, very lovely, and tried to help with my situation, after the first consultation for £635 I felt that the company was only charging this much as it was being paid out via insurance. Something didn't sit right with me about claiming that cost - free or not. The first thing offered after session one was medication for my dog to calm him down which also wasn't an idea I was keen on as I knew the issue was with an addition to our family and how he was responding to that change. He had never been on any sort of medication in the 6 years I had owned him. In the end I didn't give him the medication and he improved over a few weeks regardless. I don't know... the vet was really lovely but I'm not sure I received £635 worth of advice and support in a 1.5 hour session to justify continuing any more sessions. That coupled with the suggestion of medication straight away put me off continuing. That was my first insurance claim in 3 years, and I'll be really disappointed if my premium goes up further because of this claim.**EDIT**:Hours after submitting my review I received an email from Behavet telling me how 'incredibly upset' I had made their vet by posting my review and would I consider removing it. To comment to the further response below, the medication was collected as there was no other actionable options given other than feeding kongs and keeping him crated to rest, and with weeks of sleep deprivation because of the situation, I felt I had no other option. I decided after speaking with the vet on collection, that it wasn't essential and so he wasn't given it. Thank you.

description:
Equine America UK is a traditional, family run business, founded in 1997 by Phil and Julie Middleton and now run by their son, Lee. Wishing to maintain the trusted image of the Equine America brand, whilst moving it into the 21st century, Lee brought on board world-leading equine nutritionist Deborah Lucas MSc.Eq.S., CBiol., R.Nutr. in 2018 and moved all production from the US to the UK.  Deborah is now instrumental in the design and formulation of all Equine America products, from the original Cortaflex to an extensive range of highly effective supplements and external applications for horses, dogs, cats and people.
 
All our products are manufactured in the UK, in food industry standard factories, using only the freshest, most innovative and effective ingredients available from approved suppliers. We use state of the art, unique, fingerprint laser quality testing on every single ingredient to ensure a uniform strength and quality along with an exclusive mixing process to ensure that each scoop contains equal amounts of active ingredients. Our BETA NOPS and UFAS accreditations reassure customers that our products do not contain prohibited substances. We also comply with the regulations administered by the UK Veterinary Medicines Directorate and the Food Standards Agency.
 
Our “30-day money back guarantee” serves to reinforce the total confidence that we have in our products.

title: Ongoing issues with orders being taken…
review: Ongoing issues with orders being taken not able to provide or delayed. Several times taken order express delivery for it to be delayed. Whilst they refunded express delivery when I complained not overly helpful when it is specialist food. I had an email advising if I ordered by 19th standard delivery I would receive the order before Xmas. Placed order on the 18th express delivery to be told delivery would be 27th onwards. On contacting told reason being placed it after they closed! It was online order and still before 19th. Had just enough to last till 27th. Now been told 5 days later run out of the dry food and cancelled order. My cat has large and small bowel disease and tri tric. Without the dry food she will eat substantially more wet meaning I will now run out of wet food by the time I place another order. This food is required for medical reasons and I placed it in plenty of time to ensure I did not run out. Any other food will make my cat extremely ill. Will be looking for new supplier in New Year that is reliable once OK it happens, but this is the 4th time at least in last few months.

description:
Hey there fellow dog lovers! Let me tell you the tail (pun intended) of how our brand came to be.

It all started 3 years ago when my furry best friend Dudley had a bad reaction to a bag of shop bought treats from a well-known supermarket chain. Little did we know that the treats were chock-full of hidden nasties such as cereals, corn, sugar, derivatives, preservatives, and flavourings. It didn't take long for Dudley to develop a runny bum and a bad tummy - talk about a total paw-saster!

We rushed Dudley to our local vet who ran a few tests and discovered that he was allergic to wheat. After a lot of research, countless emails, and car miles, we finally stumbled upon a handful of fantastic natural treat suppliers who we now partner with to bring you the best of the best natural dog treats today.

But we didn't stop there. We realised that there were so many dog owners out there who were also struggling to find healthy, safe and delicious treats for their fur babies. That's when we decided to create a community of like-minded dog owners who share our passion for all things natural, nutritious and delicious.

So, we started a private customer Facebook group where dog owners could come together, interact, and share their stories, tips, and tricks. We wanted to create a space where people could feel supported, educated and empowered to make the best choices for their dogs.

And that's exactly what we did! Our community has grown into a tight-knit group of dog moms and dads who are passionate about giving their furry family members the very best. We've become a go-to resource for dog owners looking to go raw hide-free, learn more about the benefits of natural dog treats, and connect with other dog lovers who share their values.

So, whether you're a seasoned dog mom/dad or a brand new puppy parent, we're here for you. We're excited to be a part of your dog's journey and can't wait to see what the future holds. Thanks for being a part of our pack! 🐶💛

title: Company good, Star rating and review is on products received (please read)
review: For clarity, my stars are given for the products received. The company responded well to my inquiry regarding the issues I speak of below, and their delivery was fast, if a little pricey, but that's the world we're in now.These treats have all the hallmarks of natural ones, especially given their eau naturale smell! I purchased the "long lasting chew box treats" and unfortunately these were not at all long lasting. Its been stated that a "long" session for a chew is 15 minutes, apparently, but only 1 of the 5 (haven't gone through all 15 yet) has lasted more than 4 minutes - I bought this box as a test so I could stop buying the rather expensive Yakkers chew but Ive since had to go back to them in order to keep my dog still for more than a few minutes.The split antler however, was a success and lasted 3 or 4 sessions, but at 3/4 used, my Lab is no longer interested in it - Most likely cause its dried out, but that's a guess.Overall the company seems decent and I appreciate that a review of 3* for one box of treats that wasn't what I had expected could be seen as a little unfair but its currently all I have to go on, so I hope its been useful.I would use this company given their aim is to deliver natural treats to your dog, but I wouldn't expect anything different to some of the existing long chews out there.

It didn't take long for Dudley to develop a runny bum and a bad tummy - talk about a total paw-saster!

We rushed Dudley to our local vet who ran a few tests and discovered that he was allergic to wheat. After a lot of research, countless emails, and car miles, we finally stumbled upon a handful of fantastic natural treat suppliers who we now partner with to bring you the best of the best natural dog treats today.

But we didn't stop there. We realised that there were so many dog owners out there who were also struggling to find healthy, safe and delicious treats for their fur babies. That's when we decided to create a community of like-minded dog owners who share our passion for all things natural, nutritious and delicious.

So, we started a private customer Facebook group where dog owners could come together, interact, and share their stories, tips, and tricks. We wanted to create a space where people could feel supported, educated and empowered to make the best choices for their dogs.

And that's exactly what we did! Our community has grown into a tight-knit group of dog moms and dads who are passionate about giving their furry family members the very best. We've become a go-to resource for dog owners looking to go raw hide-free, learn more about the benefits of natural dog treats, and connect with other dog lovers who share their values.

So, whether you're a seasoned dog mom/dad or a brand new puppy parent, we're here for you. We're excited to be a part of your dog's journey and can't wait to see what the future holds. Thanks for being a part of our pack! 🐶💛

title: 3.5 marks from me, to be honest..
review: I am probably around the 3.5 mark for an honest review, but good points, the food looks and smells good and its easy to serve up. Two of my dogs prefer it to RAW, which is what my other three dogs eat. We have had these two of our five on DD for some time now and had to switch them from a premium raw food.   However, we are having to feed more of DD, to keep them up to a slim, healthy weight as I believe there are simply too many vegetables bulking out the recipe.  I am curious as to why there is so much cabbage topped up with other vegetables, such as Parsnips, Cauliflower and Swede, carrots, which make up approx. 26% of your recipes? This I believe is over the recommended guidelines (25% max) of how much vegetable a dog should eat, with the advise that 10% is more than ample in dog foods.  So I am curious (and a little concerned) that I might be feeding too many unnecessary vegetables and not feeding enough meat (less than 60% in your recipes) Both of mine are very active and of working breeds. I am questioning whether this diet will sustain them long term.  This is an expensive food, which unfortunately, loses some points from us, because of the high vegetable content, but feel that 'you're on to something, just not quite there yet'. I'm relieved that there is a fresh food cooked company that doesn't use legumes, Pea starch, Tapioca and beet pulp, but feel it would be more nutritional if meat protein was increased and or egg/cartilage for example were used instead.  Having said that it would most likely make it unaffordable to most consumers, if more premium ingredients were used instead and its already expensive as it is. Shame really, as I do think this is a good alternative, but imo, there is room for improvement.

title: Really disappointed and frustrated
review: Really disappointed and frustrated with this company now. My last delivery was lost and I had to chase it up to get DifferentDog to send a new delivery. Now, this month my delivery should have arrived on Friday and I’m still waiting for it on Saturday evening, only to find out it might turn up on Sunday after being dispatched on Thursday. I get that there are postal and courier delays but this is starting to be a pattern. I’m also very frustrated by the recent 10 percent price hike, plus delivery cost. Given how much I’m paying every 4 weeks for this food I honestly expect more. If there are courier issues, which the company clearly knows about, use a different courier, or send it a day earlier so I don’t run out of food. Or, simply keep customers updated in advance. Very soon, I’ll be paying close to £200 every 4 weeks to feed a medium sized dog. I do this because I like the product, but honestly I’m starting to think this company is overpriced and overrated.

title: Large chunks of fat
review: I genuinely thought I'd found the quality of food I was looking for, and my dogs seem to really enjoy it. My only problem however is the large chunks of fat that have recently featured in some of the meals (mainly Hearty Beef & Berries & Lamb Hotpot). I need to point out that these chunks of fat have been a recent thing - whilst there has always been some smaller pieces of fat in the meals (which I know is important for a balanced diet), these chunks of fat have been quite large and have been a feature of my last 2 deliveries. I reached out to Different Dog but in all honesty, I wasn't satisfied with their response. They told me that dogs are not like humans and don't eat with their eyes, that fat is important for their diet (which I wasn't disputing) and that I should feed them the chunks of fat as they are. I even sent photos to show them that these weren't small pieces, but I was told to feed them or warm them up so I couldn't see them. I don't feel comfortable in feeding big pieces of fat, and since the food has not always been like this I questioned whether they had changed ingredients, which I was told no. I'm not sure how many people would feel comfortable feeding chunks of fat either, I feel like I wasn't heard tbh when I contacted them and when you are paying a premium for quality, I don't expect that.

title: Big chunks of fat in meals
review: Like a similar review several of Daisy's dinners have had big chunks of fat in them...mainly the beef, lamb & venison. I spoke to customer service who suggested I email...which I did sending photos of each meal that had the chunks of fat in along with the type & batch number...I received a patronising response stating these are fatty meats ( I'm aware of this) that they are wild animals & their diet varies through the seasons so there will be a higher fat content at different times of the year. This was the just of the response. Absolutely gutted as I like this company they're easy to deal with & Daisy who it a faddy eater likes the food. I don't subscribe but do order regular probably each month & I spend a lot of money...very loyal to the product & have recommended to many friends prior to the excess fat issue who are all subscribers...I'm an animal rescuer & I've consistently told all of my animal friends how great the food is. My point is I've been having diff dog for some time at least a year maybe more & this never used to happen...seriously its a recent thing of the last few months...As your customer care person said of course you expect to have some fat in meat especially those Daisy prefers...However not this much...I've literally just photographed a piece of fat about an inch in diameter along with several other big chunks. This is unacceptable. As is your response. I hate complaining but this is wrong...Daisy's a small dog who cannot digest this level of fat nor should she...So I'm picking it out for her...Again this is recent never had this issue before & I see someone else has. I will say it doesn't happen all of the time but I'd say at least in 10 out of 30 meals it's now happening. I don't want to stop buying diff dog as Daisy loves it...I want the responsible considerate response & the issue to be addressed by you otherwise I will have to. Very upset & dissatisfied customer right now.

description:
We offer 100% natural dog chews & treats!

We are careful and very conscious when it comes to sourcing our products.

Our dogs are part of our family. We know they deserve nothing less than the best. But in reality, most dog chews and treats have big marketing budgets but inferior quality. Also, most dog chews & treats advertise as "natural", but they come from Asia with uncertain, unknown and often harmful ingredients, produced under poor environmental and labour standards and cost a lot. Commercially available chews left a lot to desire. Eventually, after much trial and error, we realised that fresh and natural treats worked best for dogs.
We don't like eating junk food, so why should things be different for our four-legged family members? Our chews & treats are suitable for dogs with sensitive tummies. Many commercial dog chews & treats do not suit many dogs, so we researched the different types of chews and treats. Our sourcing products are either UK or EU-produced. We visit our suppliers and talk to them regularly to ensure that our products are 100% natural, with no added additives, chemicals, or flavourings. Also, these companies follow EU laws regarding animal welfare.
Today, we are proud to offer an exciting line of dog chews and treats made from a single or limited ingredient, 100% natural and as nutritious as delicious. 100% satisfaction guaranteed.

Let your Dog be a Dog. Unlock his natural instincts the healthy way!

title: Claire is fantastic
review: My dog is nervous due to past traumatic experiences at another vet clinic. Apex has been amazing for the most part.  Claire is spectacular with my dog, she takes the time to fuss over her and reassure her that it’s not a scary place and her confidence is building slowly but surely. This was set back previously by one of the other vets in this practice who didn’t explain anything to me and shoved a muzzle on my very anxious dog with no prior warning when she was hiding in the corner of the room. My dog got so distressed that her nose started bleeding with the muzzle on and I had to take it off. I do appreciate any dog under distress could be a cause for concern for a vet but the way this was previously handled was completely unacceptable and set her back again, this vet didn’t seem to care. Unsure if it was because of her breed or if there was another issue at the time. If it had been explained to me that a muzzle would be recommended then I would have put it on her myself with great care and not shove it on her face with force when she’s trembling in the corner with fear. I would now only go to Claire as she is so calm and good with my dog that we’re building up trust again (not.a muzzle in sight!) Overall knowing I will never make an appointment with the other vet I am very happy with the care provided. Reception staff are welcoming and friendly both on the phone and face to face.

description: Local, Independent, 24 hours companion animal veterinary surgery in Denny (Near Falkirk,) Scotland. Dedicated to the health and wellbeing of your pet. 24 hour emergency service is available.  Where your pet is part of our family.
title: Beware - owners’ opinions not welcome!
review: My dog was in the practice to receive his vaccination for the year. He also had an ear check and the vet found they were a little swollen so prescribed anti inflammatory medication ear drops. My dog was quite distressed when in the vet consultation room and the vet did not demonstrate to me how to put the ear drops in (if she would have done so I would have recognised that my dog would not have allowed me to put them in).Once I got home, I tried to administer and my dog became very distressed, would not allow me to administer. I persevered and kept trying for two days, tried two of us, tried a different person trying to administer but still he was quite distressed.I phoned Apex on the Saturday and asked if I could bring the ear drops back in exchange for another treatment. The nurse on the phone told me I should bring my dog in for a demonstration on how to put the ear drops in, I explained I did not require a demonstration as I knew how to administer, the problem was that my dog did not want me to administer them.I asked to simply swap for another alternative treatment. I explained he had just been seen by the vet. The nurse told me she could not offer this unless I brought my dog in and paid for a consultation and alternative treatment - I had just been in the practice two days prior and paid for treatment which if the vet would have tried to put in my dogs ear, she would have known my dog would not tolerate. Dissatisfied, I felt the practice were just trying to make money from me and felt very uneasy about the situation so put the phone down and went back to trying another method of putting my dogs ear drops in. Luckily, a distraction technique worked (for anyone struggling- try to administer whilst your dog is waiting at the door to go out for a walk/to the garden).My dog is seen nearly every two months to have his glands emptied, we are always straight on the phone to the vet if anything is wrong, we are probably on the phone to the vets a little too much! But want to make sure he is looked after as he is like our child! We would pay for anything he needed - but we felt we were being taken advantage of in this case.My faith was shattered in the practice from then on - at the beginning I thought I had found a genuinely great practice but unfortunately, the owner shattered it even more on the Monday following my phone call with the nurse.On Monday, I found an email in my inbox from the owner asking me to call him to speak about his concerns which the nurse had escalated to him. The owner had asked me to work with him to “better understand each other” and “take feedback”.So, I sent a very detailed email allowing him my feedback on what I though was handled wrongly, what I thought could have been said better, even giving my opinion on what the nurse could have said on the phone.I felt that the nurse was very condescending on the phone and let the owner know this on my emails. He let me know that he had worked with the nurse in question for over 11 years and he had never heard her being condescending over the phone. This may be the case, however, to basically make out like I am lying about her sounding condescending is very unprofessional and I really did not appreciate this from the owner.He let me know that if I had spoken with him on the Saturday, he would have waived the fee. However, the nurse never mentioned any of this on the phone.I ended my emails by asking why, if they had known and worked with one another for 11 years, had the nurse not offered to exchange my dogs ear drops for an alternative - waiving the fee?For asking this question, and offering my feedback - which the owner did ask for on several occasions - my dog was banned from the practice.In all my years of being a pet owner, in fact in all my years of dealing with ANY business at all I have NEVER experienced bad customer service like it.So, BEWARE, if you feel strongly about anything, or have an opinion… be careful you may be banned from the practice for sharing it.

description:
Collared Creatures was born out of a passion of all things dog. We make a full range of beautiful and simply styled, luxury handmade dog accessories for the home and outdoors.

We started our business way back in 2014, it grew from wanting to find beautiful dog collars for our dogs, that was practical and hardwearing but didn’t compromise on style – we really struggled, so we decided to make our own collars.

One passion led to another and before we knew it our family, friends, and the local neighbourhood started to ask us if we could make collars and leads for them too – and before long, we were making our first ever Dog Cave Bed and very own Dog Drying Coats!

Eight years on, we’re proud to have expanded, to offer a full range of beautiful and simply styled, luxury handmade dog accessories for the home and outdoors.

We offer doting dog lovers an exclusive range: Luxury Dog Beds, Luxury Blankets and Sofa Throws, stunning Dog Collars & Leads, and Practical Dog Drying Coats.

We delighted to have also launched our own bespoke Signature Collections of different styled Dog Collars and Leads.

Collared Creatures are a small and family run, independent British Business.

Our business is all about ‘Nurturing Love’, making products that create special moments for you and your dog and helping you build that amazing dog and owner bond.

We take the time to source the finest quality materials and constantly perfect our product designs to deliver real comfort, ideal fit and practicality – giving you dog accessories that keep your dog feeling warm, safe and utterly loved.

At collared creatures our mission is to provide fellow dog lovers with the finest range of beautiful products for your pooches! We have a great selection of beds to make sure your furry companions feel safe, cosy & warm. We also have a large selection of exquisite hand crafted collars & leads.

We’re inspired every day, by designing beautiful and gorgeous dog accessories for you and your dog to enjoy in the home and wear on outdoor adventures.

Following our passion for dogs and doing what we truly love makes every day special for us.

We understand dogs and how delighted owners are when they see their dogs having a soft and cosy bed to rest and relax in, collars that make feel safe and dog drying coats that get their dog dry, warmed up quickly and feeling cosy.

Like you, we cherish the strong bond that we have with our dogs and love nothing more than to create those special moments for you to share with you dog too.

Take a look at our collections of luxury handmade dog collars and leads, cosy and warm dog beds, our luxuriously soft dog blankets and our perfectly practical dog clothing.
title: Fantastic bed and collar
review: I bought a bed and biothane collar. I sort happy with both products. As described and while pricey, they are both excellent quality and worth the money. My puppy is not a good sleeper and very fussy when it comes to getting comfortable. She loves her bed and it has really helped with getting her to sleep for longer stretches in the night.

title: Cave bed not suitable but good quality
review: Good quality beds, but unfortunately even the large cave bed is not suitable for our medium size gsp. The base is big enough, but the hood is low so he would need to crawl into the bed, which he isn’t going to do. Probably OK for small dogs who would be able to walk into the bed. Kept the bed as posting back would have been a hassle and it is good quality with plenty of filling in the base, but have just half zipped the hood without the foam/wire in it and arranged the hood as a raised side around part of the bed. Wouldn’t order the cave bed again as could get a good quality bed with sides for less. Like the tartan fabric.

Would order from again would just appreciate more communication next time :)

Eight years on, we’re proud to have expanded, to offer a full range of beautiful and simply styled, luxury handmade dog accessories for the home and outdoors.

We offer doting dog lovers an exclusive range: Luxury Dog Beds, Luxury Blankets and Sofa Throws, stunning Dog Collars & Leads, and Practical Dog Drying Coats.

We delighted to have also launched our own bespoke Signature Collections of different styled Dog Collars and Leads.

Collared Creatures are a small and family run, independent British Business.

Our business is all about ‘Nurturing Love’, making products that create special moments for you and your dog and helping you build that amazing dog and owner bond.

We take the time to source the finest quality materials and constantly perfect our product designs to deliver real comfort, ideal fit and practicality – giving you dog accessories that keep your dog feeling warm, safe and utterly loved.

At collared creatures our mission is to provide fellow dog lovers with the finest range of beautiful products for your pooches! We have a great selection of beds to make sure your furry companions feel safe, cosy & warm. We also have a large selection of exquisite hand crafted collars & leads.

We’re inspired every day, by designing beautiful and gorgeous dog accessories for you and your dog to enjoy in the home and wear on outdoor adventures.

Following our passion for dogs and doing what we truly love makes every day special for us.

We understand dogs and how delighted owners are when they see their dogs having a soft and cosy bed to rest and relax in, collars that make feel safe and dog drying coats that get their dog dry, warmed up quickly and feeling cosy.

Like you, we cherish the strong bond that we have with our dogs and love nothing more than to create those special moments for you to share with you dog too.

Take a look at our collections of luxury handmade dog collars and leads, cosy and warm dog beds, our luxuriously soft dog blankets and our perfectly practical dog clothing.

description:
Find An Emergency Vet
Pet Care Advice
Customer Hub



About Vets Now 


Pet emergencies can happen at any time – including when your regular vet is closed.
That’s why our nationwide network of out-of-hours pet emergency clinics are open through the night, at weekends and on bank holidays, so we’re ready and waiting to provide expert pet emergency care when your regular vet is having some time off.

Our pet emergency clinics are the pet equivalent of A&E and our purpose is to give you and your pet the care and support you deserve, at the time you need it most, whether it’s four in the morning or in the middle of Sunday lunch.
Vets Now provides this trusted service to more than 1000 veterinary practices across the UK — from over 60 dedicated out-of-hours clinics and two 24/7 pet emergency hospitals. In total, we treat around 200,000 small animals every year — our highly-skilled team works hard throughout the night, weekends and Bank Holidays. So whether you’re in Aberdeen, Belfast or Portsmouth we’re there for you and your pet when you need us most.
We’ve also pioneered other ways to help pets, pet owners and the veterinary profession, such as our comprehensive referrals service and providing our staff with industry-leading training and development opportunities. We also support the pet blood transfusion charity, Pet Blood Bank UK. Meanwhile, our two hospitals — in Glasgow and Manchester — are home to some of the UK’s leading specialists in the field of emergency and critical care and provide care 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

title: Patronising and abrupt vet!
review: I've given three stars on the basis that our dog was seen very promptly and the receptionist was lovely.  We took our dog to the vet following her first seizure so to say we were worried is an understatement,The vet we saw had a very abrupt almost uncaring attitude and seemed more interested in showing us harnesses that she thought we should buy from a website/company we'd never heard of.  She also made quite a big issue about our dog being overweight and said she needed to lose a kg which then went to 1.5kg and then said "if people say she's skinny she's the right weight".Had she been going for a regular check up then I probably wouldn't have minded but when you are paying £350,  I don't expect to hear things like "that's an awful harness - mind you,  you aren't to know".To be clear my dog spends a lot of time in and out of the vets as she receives immunotherapy,  so is regularly weighed and has been wearning the same harness for two years.  At no point has any vet ever said she needs to lose weight,  nor have they ever commented about her harness.Maybe it's me but when I see a vet for my dogs I want to feel that they genuinely care for animals.  This vet didn't give me that impression at all and seemed more interested in making unhelpful comments,  completely unrelated to the purpose of our visit.

I lost another dog just 2 weeks previously and the care & compassion from my own vet practice was outstanding. There was no offer ofmemory making with yourselves, fortunately the pet crematorium did this for me. With the outrageous prices being charged, this is the least you could have done.

title: SmartTrace Registration
review: Firstly I should say that I agree with a lot of people, that the lack of a Contact Number (for SmartTrace Customer Services) is counterproductive in my opinion. Sure enough, the SmartTrace site now showed a 'pending' Transfer and on 20th June, the Transfer was completed!It's a difficult one to 'Rate' because although the Registration process  leaves a lot to be desired, once a 'human being' got involved, it went very smoothly - surprise, surprise - (Ref initial comment on Contact Number!).Anyway, I think 3/5 is fair.

review: I HAVE SINCE RESOLVED MATTERS WITH THIS COMPANY AND THEY WERE VERY FAIR.  HOWEVER I DID HAVE 1 POINT REGARDING REFUNDS WHICH I HAD TO ARGUE.   THE PERSON REPLYING WAS VERY POLITE AND RESPONDED DAILY.  I HAVE BEEN ISSUED WITH A REFUND OF MY POSTAGE AND PACKAGING FOR WHICH I AM GRATEFUL .....I ordered itch for my 2 cats, I have used flea treatments for 20 years , I decided to give this new company a go as they wete offering a free trial. Stef the vet called first thing on the morning I’d decided it was time to let wolf go. She worked round us for the best time to come out, she eased my worries and was so very kind on the phone. Stef then came out that morning and was lovely. She gave us space when we needed it and explained everything that was going to happen. Stef handled Wolf with such care. The only thing I would have changed is wolfs first injection made him a little upset but then injections aren’t nice for anyone.After his first injection that sedated him he fell into a peaceful sleep and felt no more pain. He was fast asleep when the final injection was given and felt nothing when he passed dying peacefully in my arms surrounded by family and our other dog frank. Stef was so very good with us. She cleaned wolf up, cut some of his fur for us for a keepsake and wrapped him beautifully in one of his favourite blankets ready for him to take his final journey to the crematorium. title: Left without an answer
review: We contacted Dignipets on Monday evening as we needed support to make an incredibly tough decision to put our beloved family dog of 14 years to sleep. My partner had previously called them for advice and they’d been reasonably helpful so we took this route again after our usual vet recommended this also as they had no emergency appointments. We called Dignipets on Monday evening and were advised that they couldn’t get through to the vet/person they needed but, someone would call us back. We never received a phone call. To this day, on Friday, we’ve still not received a call. Thankfully we found a local vet (Medivet Oakengates who were exceptional) who contacted us within 30 minutes to carry out this tough decision. Whilst I appreciate services are busy, to not receive even a courtesy call to let us know they were unable to support, when you’re discussing decisions of this nature is poor. It’s really distressed my Grandmother, whose dog was the poor dog in question as she felt that Dignipets didn’t care about her beloved friend as should be expected by an animal/veterinary service. I think it’s important for this to be raised so it can be investigated as to whether this is standard within your service and if so, whether it can be addressed to avoid upset for others in the future. I appreciate that this may have been a one off experience but, I feel compelled to share as I can’t imagine it’s something you would want a repeat of as a service.

title: Terrible experience with the cargo company at destination
review: (Update)-------------------------------------------------------------Quickly after raising my concerns, Airpets contacted me. As the reply to that review, they do not have control over which cargo company handle the pets once at destination, the airline companies do. So, British Airways was the airline company my pets flew with, and they use Mercury Cargo.For information, the Mercury Cargo warehouse is also IAG Cargo so if the airline company you use work with them, your pets will be handle like freight shipments not live animals. -------------------------------------------------------------(Previous review below)I shipped my pets with Airpets from London to Los Angeles. While they are very nice and professional people (friendly when I dropped my cats, offered me to send me updates through WhatsApp), nobody mentioned how pets are handled at Mercury Cargo (company they work with at destination, LAX).  Prior to the travel, I was told by email by a Mercury representative to come get the paperwork at 1930 the day of the flight, go get a stamp from the U.S. Customs and come back to pick up my cats. So, I did come at 1930 to get my paperwork, and they told me to come back at 2100 as it was not ready. Additionally, no one explained to me that I had to sign up to "get in line". The pets are NOT kept in a climate controlled room and they are left on wooden palettes in the middle of forklift machine moving freight around, in a freight warehouse not an live animal allocated room.The great reputation Airpets has might be because they often take care of the entire trip, which means pets owners get their pets at their door and so they don't see this. My cats peed themselves (which did not happened on longer trip in the past) and were in shock to have been handled the way they were handled, plus they were waiting next to crates with barking dogs (I understand that the dogs barked, I love dogs. They were crying as they saw their owners waiting). Why would Airpets people be so amazing and do such a great job at departure to then allow such situation at destination? I do not understand.

title: Repatriating Guinea pigs UK to Canada
review: I am repatriating to Canada at the end of August and I had to get my three guinea pigs home. Trying to sort this whole process in the middle of a pandemic was an absolute nightmare as most of the airlines that usually fly guinea pigs as animal cargo weren’t taking any animal bookings, but airpets made the process quite easy and a lot less stressful. I dealt with Jake and he was an excellent agent and very helpful. I will admit I was quite demanding and definitely not the easiest customer to be dealing with due to the stress of trying to plan a move and the repatriation of my pigs during a pandemic, so I was a bit of a nightmare myself, but Jake was very understanding of the circumstances and was always as polite and helpful as possible. The process was actually very simple once we got the airline to agree to fly the pigs (that was the hardest part), and it was very straightforward. Thankfully my province didn’t require any kind of special import permits for rodents so I just had to deal with the documentation airpets sent and then the vet certification, all of which was easy to do/obtain. Make sure to check with the Canadian Food Inspection Agency about whether or not you need permits for your animals based on their final destination. There were some issues with the airline/Vancouver airport facilities which made it more stressful than necessary, but those were mostly due to COVID complications and were not the fault of Jake or airpets. However, DO take into consideration that most airlines are not flying regular schedules or taking advanced bookings at the moment because of potential schedule changes. I was only able to officially book their travel 14 days before the travel date for these reasons, but as I had been in contact with Jake since June it was very straightforward once we were allowed to book as I had already completed all the necessary documents. But do be aware that there are delays and changes with the airlines themselves. Also, there may be extra fees from the airline/airport facilities that will be added to the already hefty sum of animal cargo. Flying any animal(s), no matter how small, is very expensive. It’s the safest bet to add a bit more money to your budget in case of extra fees. I wasn’t aware of some of the fees until booking as they came from the airport facilities and were affected by the route the pigs were flying. When I arrived at their offices on the morning of their flight I was given as much time as I needed to personally set up their kennel how I wanted it and say goodbye, and was not rushed by any of the employees who all seemed genuinely interested in the pigs and wanted to know about them. I’m very thankful I wasn’t rushed because I was very anxious about them travelling, especially as they were going on a few days ahead of me and being picked up by family upon arrival. The environment was calming and I didn’t feel any pressure to speed up, even though they obviously had a schedule to keep to. They were very good about this and I appreciate it greatly. I was informed via email when their flight took off from LHR and then was sent photos the following morning (due to time difference) of them in their stayover cage at the Vancouver airport facilities (their domestic connection was the next day), which was very reassuring. The only reason I haven’t given 5/5 stars is because there was no information given to me about collection and I had to ask when and where they were supposed to be collected right before they arrived, but otherwise everything went smoothly and better than I imagined. I gave Jake an update (per request) once they were collected and he seemed very happy that they had arrived safely. The pigs arrived safely and seemed only mildly peeved about the long travel (two flights ~13h total plus a stayover) and are happy and healthy and were eating their food and exploring their temporary set up as soon as they got home. A bonus is that the Canada customs charge for my province was a lot lower than expected. They are apparently acting like their normal selves and seem to be otherwise unaffected. I couldn’t find any reviews about Guinea pigs/small animals flying with airpets so I thought this might be helpful to anyone else who may have to travel with their small animals. I was very weary about them travelling despite having read other peoples’ stories about travelling with their pigs and them being fine, but as I couldn’t find a review for airpets about guinea pigs I was very anxious. I hope this might ease someone else’s anxiety in the future. Overall I would highly recommend airpets to anyone needing to move their pets out of the UK as they tried to make the process as stress free as possible for me despite the whole situation being an absolute nightmare. Thank you so much airpets and Jake!

title: We chose Airpets for the relocation of our French Bulldog from the UK to the USA
review: We chose Airpets for the relocation of our French Bulldog.  We moved from the UK to Pennsylvania in the US.  We felt that after reading the reviews, seeing the Instagram page and after talking to ..., that they would be perfect.  Some issues were out of their hands such as the heatwave that hit all 3 airports our pup would have to go through - LDN Heathrow; Turkey and IAD Washington.  The communication from ... at Airpets was not consistent and we would have to initiate all contact.  We saw that this had been picked up on in some previous reviews.  Once dates had been set, Airpets were good enough to collect our pup from a new location as we had already moved to the US.  He was collected on time and the vet check was done quickly with emails sent to confirm this.  The A-Z Broker kept us informed.  We were disappointed with the photos we received.  Reviews all comment on the great photos and videos.    All we got were some photos of him looking unhappy and eating from a food bowl that had been left in his wee patch.  We understand that he was flying with the Turkish Air handlers, but Airpets states strongly about their good rapport with all airlines handling the transport.  This did not feel like that at all.  Almost as though once he left Heathrow Airpets were not bothered.  Choice Aviation handled the last stage and we were appalled at how we were re-united with our pup.  He was left in his crate with a view of us, he was crying and howling.  Despite being an hour early to pick him up and the flight running 58 minutes late, Choice Aviation were unhelpful and did not appear to know what they were doing.  We were made to wait and fill out paperwork that could have been done earlier, the staff dealing with us had no idea how to use the system, in the meantime our pup was getting distressed and we were not allowed in to see him.  A lovely member of staff came to our rescue and went to comfort our pup, then took over to complete the release quickly.  Thank goodness he knew what he was doing.  We were then given another issue and that was getting him out of the crate.  He had been cable tied in, understandable, but we were told that they could not cut the ties or give us anything to open it.  My husband ended up ripping them off with brute force.  To end it all we then had to rush our pup into a public toilet and wash him in the sink.  Where he had got so distressed he ended up covered in his own feces.  We expected after a 10 hour flight he would need a clean up, but not to this extend.  Overall we are disappointed with the image that Airpets paints for itself as we feel we saw none of this.  Jake stepped in at the last minute as ... was ill, his communication was better but did not make up for the whole experience.  My husband is currently putting a complaint together direct to Airpets.

title: Transiting through LHR
review: This was the 4th pet agent quote I got and it seemed reasonable plus good reviews online. I was travelling from Iceland and just forced to transit  through London to Ireland because of covid.If I was reviewing on just exports I would give 10stars and full credit to Lee Fisher as he did a great job prompt clear and detailed quote, fast reponse emails, last minute change to crate dimensions and he delt with it professionally without a problem for me, even taking after hour call to confirm payment etc for travel the following day. Imports email agent replies were slower and caused me a lot of unnecessary stress on the actual day of travel. Because of covid I had a logistical nightmare of balancing days and the pet agents didn't believe me when I tried to explain it so here it is. New covid rules since June 8th meant I had to be in and out of the UK again within 24hrs so dog and I were booked to fly the next morning because there wasn't enough time to clear him between same day flights . Iceland doesn't issue eu passports because they are not in the EU only health certs, you can't collect that until the dog has had the worm dose within 5days of travel needing to factor in the 24hrs extra to get to Ireland for the health cert to be valid til final destination. And only two flights per week out of Iceland plus the vet is closed except emergency and the dept of agriculture also closed over the weekend.  I had prechecked myself with the dept of agriculture in Iceland, the UK and Ireland and all said health cert was valid even for transiting through the uk. I should have checked with the animal reception center at Heathrow because officials there claimed it was an outdated annex/health cert and not suitable insisting on getting  the UK pet passport issued but this was not made clear to me until I called the animal reception center myself. The Airpets agent emailed at lunch to say dog has arrived and is a bit thirsty but all OK. 30mins later she messaged me to say they can't find all of the dogs paperwork (which icelandair cargo had taped to the crate) I didn't get a reply so 30mins passed and I sent another email and got a reply from a guy called Jake to say the authorities at larc were not happy with the paperwork(oked by the vet in Iceland and I had to go to the department of agriculture in Iceland for the final document all oked by them) and needed confirmation from the vet on iceland. -This new agent did his best with the mess he was handed. He was my only point of contact in the company on the day and unable to tell me exactly what was needed but he did give me contact phone numbers which enabled me to get it all sorted eventually. This became a time sensitive issue it was now 4pm and at 5:30pm the out of hours vet charges kicked in. The vet secretary in Iceland could not find the rabies vaccine number,I resent the copy to her I had given to Airpets already. The arc wanted a new document signed by the vet who was out on an emergency call. I spent from 3:30-8pm between phonecalls and emails to the vet in Iceland to the animal reception center and to Airpets. The pet agents clock off at 5:30 also and the manager Lee has the out of hours phone and he had a day off. He wanted to change the flight to another day later and do it all in office hours. Not listening to me when I said it could have been done within office hours today and I am supposed to go into 2week quarantine and I live 5 hours from Dublin Airport so the next day travel was not an option for me. He didn't like my tone, he had his first day off in three weeks, and nobody at the pet agents was responsible for this avoidable mess or willing to do what I had hired them to do -Get my dog from the Icelandair plane to the aerlingus plane on the date planned and as requested. Between 3pm and 8pm I had to call and call to get the information needed so my dog would travel with me as planned. Around 7pm after 4hours of asking, demanding,a little shouting and begging I just broke down crying on the phone to Lee F who had wasted his evening trying to persuade me otherwise. He went into the office on his day off and sorted the whole thing within 20mins. Again, full points for his work but the evening was unnecessary and a total waste for all involved. If I knew at 2pm exactly what was needed I could have helped the vet in Iceland. It worked out really expensive for me 720pounds for something that should have cost a lot less. I am sure they are a good company just there were delays and changes on my side plus this outdated annex nonesence and not enough active staff in airpets on the day I needed them. They need a seperate out of hours duty manager to ensure continuity and so the manager can take a day off. And in all the pet agencies they have seperate import and export agents rather than one case worker taking responsibility. In the end my dog travelled as planned and I aged considerably.

title: Sadly disappointing
review: We had hoped to write a glowing review of Airpets, they had impressed us in the early stages of the process, but unfortunately our dog's journey to Canada was not what we had expected and their subsequent handling of the concerns we raised did not feel appropriate.  We were not given any information or paperwork to enable us to collect our dog on arrival at Calgary.  This meant there were delays and a lot of running around once we landed before we could collect our boy.  This was incredibly stressful, after an eight hour flight, for both us and our dog, and could have been avoided.  When we raised this matter with Airpets they said they had recommended using a Canadian agent in their early paperwork, that we had received some months before.  We should also have been provided with an emergency contact number, that we didn't have and there appears to have been a little bit of slight of hand with the truth regarding the sending of customs documents (Airpets said they sent them, we didn't receive).  When we raised our concerns with Airpets they were slow to respond and only gave us a full answer after being chased.  This was disappointing as it suggested a lax approach to after-care. I have read the glowing reviews of Airpets and this is one of the reasons we are so disappointed with the service we received.  It appears they can do an exceptional job when the right people are working on your case, but when the wrong people are involved, there is a general lack of responsibility and communication.  This is the first time we have taken a pet on a plane with us, and we made this abundantly clear to our agent at Airpets, the assumption however was that we would manage a lot of the arrival matters ourselves and would somehow know how to navigate the customs process.

title: Some good aspects but overall service very poor
review: We booked AirPets to help fly our dog from England to Colombia a couple of months ago. They were one of the more reasonably priced options that we found and we were immediately assigned an agent to support us with the process. Communication wasn't fantastic with this agent, while they always responded promptly, I had to do a lot of chasing to find out what was happening and I felt I was only supplied information when I asked for it whereas I would have liked the agent to be more pro active. When it came to our dog actually flying Airpets were great in their communication around both collecting her and how she was doing at Heathrow airport. However, communication was non existent during her journey (she had a night over in Spain before flying on to Colombia) and when she arrived in Bogota she was left in her travel crate over night without being allowed out to go to the toilet and from what we could see when we collected her, with no food or water. It then took us 5 hours to get her out of the airport the next day due to a very inefficient Colombian process, during which time our dog remained in her travel crate and became very distressed. It was my understanding that the service we were paying for would cover the moment she was collected from me until the moment my husband collected her at the other end. Be warned that this is not the case. Once your pet leaves England, you will not hear from Airpets at all and it appears they do not maintain responsibility for them. When I looked back through all the communication we had received from airpets, in the first email they sent my husband with a quote, they recommended arranging a Colombian agent to help speed along the process at the airport here but this was never mentioned again once we had engaged their services and I would have expected our travel agent to offer to help with this, especially if it was important to guaranteeing our dogs well being during the journey. Overall we were very disappointed with the service received and would not recommend them.

review: Airpets….This is my honest review of airpets.At the end of the day they did get my 17kg dog from England to Australia but that is about the only positive really. This has been the most stressful time for myself, trying to get my dog to Australia & I thought by going with a well known company I would avoid any unnecessary stress. I thought wrong. It takes 5 minutes to send an email to say your on holiday and give me someone else’s contact.Whenever I did manage to get hold of Lee Fisher, I felt like he didn’t care about my worries & that he really couldn’t be bothered.When all the vet visits were done, and pick up day arrived a man in a black van showed up at my house, I had no idea who he was & all he was wearing was a grey tracksuit. ( he turned out to be more friendly then airpets & answered all the questions he could) but I was expecting a big white van with airpets written on the side of it, cost me £155 for this service, honestly wish I took her myself now, would have saved £105. As soon as my dog was put on the plane I think I’ve had one email but that was just saying that someone else is in charge of her now, Which is obviously very reassuring for me and my family.Haven't heard from them since, they haven’t asked if she’s okay or how she’s doing in Australia.Honestly, I would like some kind of refund, they had £250 off me for doing all this & whatever else was left over from my £3600 & I felt so unwelcome & ignored the whole year of so I’ve been dealing with them.I would never use them again & would never tell anyone to use them.

description: Established at London Heathrow airport 1966, Airpets quickly grew to become the UK's leading pet travel agency.   Over fifty years later, Airpets remains a family run buisness ...
title: Only ‘ok’ barely.
review: Only ‘ok’ barely.The positives:- cat arrived safely in Dubai, so technically speaking they did what they said- the price was reasonable, not the cheapest but not the most expensive either- Airpets arranged the vet checks and forms needed without any issuesThe negatives:- complete lack of communication. Our cat had to isolate for 2 weeks due to regulations from the destination country. During the 2 weeks we received zero updates voluntarily from Airpets, and after chasing from our side 2 or 3 times we received 2 or 3 poor quality photos of our cat looking terrified hiding in a box, and that’s all we got during the whole 2 weeks she was there. As pet owners can imagine, it was quite a tense time and it does not take more than 30 seconds to snap a photo of her every 2 or 3 days without having to be constantly chased, to put owners minds at ease.- also no notice to let us know she had arrived safely (she was collected by airpets driver). No notice to say she had settled. Or that she was eating or using her litter tray. Or that she was playing or getting some exercise now and again. Nothing. Total silence except for those few photos when we chased a lot.- poor communication again. I could not get through to our contact at Airpets for the majority of the day despite attempting to call multiple times and sending multiple emails. I was simply told everyone involved is busy every time I called (but I was still receiving email responses in between from the same people who were too busy to take a call). This was when we had been told suddenly there is no direct flight and I was desperate to speak to someone to work out what alternatives we have for further boarding / different airlines etc (see next point).- poor planning and organization.We were specifically informed in writing there were direct flights available to our destination. I had heard this might not be the case due to covid and asked Airpets to reconfirm, and was told again in certain terms in writing that there are direct flights. 6 days before the scheduled departure and halfway through the quarantine isolation at AirPets facility we were told ‘there are no direct flights due to the type of aircraft BA is using on this route during covid, you can pay 2100 pounds for a pallet, or wait and hope BA change their aircraft type (despite covid) or take an indirect flight’. This was extremely disappointing and upsetting. It was too late for us to take our cat back, and we cannot pay 2100 for a pallet. Based on the confirmations we had received prior to booking with Airpets we had proceeded with all our planning. Our cat is an exotic breed snub nose and every flight is risky we definitely did not want 2 flights for her. In the end we had no realistic option but to go for the indirect flights (thankfully she was ok and luckily the weather in the Middle East was unseasonably cool during those few days).So in conclusion ok price, ok delivery for the basic requirements, but definitely don’t expect any communication or regular updates at all, and if you are making any critical arrangements based on information you’re getting from Airpets, make sure to directly call the airlines or other people involved to confirm the AirPets comments are correct before you rely on them or plan around them. We got quite fortunate with the alternative flight availability and luckily our cat got through 2 flights ok but it was quite a stressful few days. On a final note, not a single apology from Airpets when their mistake was discovered (a very ‘couldn’t give a damn’ attitude throughout) and not a single follow up or comment to advise our cat had been loaded or received at the airport. By comparison several of the other relocation companies in the Uk were super communicative and friendly but we couldn’t use them due to their lack of availability for our dates (understandably, they were booked up first). I would try one of the others first before settling on Airpets.

title: What's happened to Zooplus? Get rid of Evri!
review: I've been a loyal customer of Zooplus for almost a decade now, and am now actively seeking an alternative supplier for food and litter for my four cats due to recent poor service. My first order, placed on the 24th of November, was cancelled without any communication from Zooplus - it just suddenly appeared as Cancelled on the app when I went to check why I hadn't received it yet. The second, placed on Dec 2nd, 'arrived' today. Evri abandoned it at a random address on a different street nearby for the third time, and my partner and I have just spent the past 30 minutes driving around before finally locating it. The third, placed on Dec 5th (I was getting desperate at this point), has yet to go anywhere or do anything. What's going on, Zooplus? Given the time of year, I've been willing to overlook the slower than usual deliveries, but having to creep around my neighbours' houses trying to find parcels that have been 'delivered' by Evri is too much. My address is not difficult to find, Evri just doesn't care. STOP USING EVRI. You used to offer DPD as an alternative, and I willingly spent the extra money every time I ordered to be sure I got DPD rather than Evri. That option is no longer available. I will not order from Zooplus again if Evri is still the only delivery option. I'll willingly pay more, elsewhere, to be sure my delivery actually shows up. Edit: Zooplus contacted me directly to address this issue, and I feel they handled my complaint exceptionally. My order was compensated, they reached out to Evri to make sure no 'leave in safe place' option was acceptable at my address, and followed up on the cancelled order's refund status promptly. I'm very happy with how Zooplus has handled this, now they just need to give Evri the boot and go back to DPD!

title: I really do love tails.com as I start…
review: I really do love tails.com as I start this review. It has been a brilliant company for food for my dogs and the food has digested well by them. Furthermore, the CS is fantastic, and I have used them ongoing no fuss with three years of loyalty.The reason I am now leaving 3 stars and this can be subject to change depending on feedback. But given the rising costs over the past year or so, it's getting quite pricey to afford the food. My dogs don't settle as well with their kibble so I usually order only the wet food - my biggest complaint is that in the past tails.com have responded to me stating that they don't just do wet food offers as that is not their specialism. However I do disagree that due to the growing market of dog food, I have seen their wet food being promptly sold on the shelves. It would be incredibly benefical if tails.com could take into account their consumers who wish to purchase only their wet food but at a more affordable cost.This could be treated as a running subscription equally with fair discount. Or otherwise, something auto set-up so we don't have to always check to order. I just don't think it's very fair that myself should miss out on a fair price given that my dogs don't settle well with their kibble. Likewise, there should be a loyalty system now. There are many other companies employing this type of structure to makes things more affordable and stick to brand loyalty.Side note: Again feels incredibly unfair to constantly pay postage for the wet food amount I order. You really should be offering the chance over a certain amount to have free delivery. Little things do add up.

description:
From modest beginnings in Enfield as a single store in 1971, Jollyes has now grown into one of the leading pet food superstores with over 100 locations across the UK alongside a market-leading position in Northern Ireland.

From Perth to Plymouth, Newry to Norwich, at Jollyes customers can find anything for their pet, from pet food, pet toys and an array of pet accessories.
Customers are actively encouraged to bring their pets into store, while customers shop because Jollyes people are passionate about pets.

Potty about puppies and crazy for cats, no matter what the animal, store colleagues are always on hand to help with anything from product advice, to picking the perfect pet and accessories.

Many stores also run community clinics offering vaccinations and other advice from trained vets. And if one of Jollyes stores isn’t close by, there’s helpful advice on Jollyes website where you can ask the expert. 

Jollyes was named 2023 Pet Retail Chain of the Year at the Pet Industry Federation Awards and was named best retailer under £250m turnover in the 2024 Retail Week awards.  Earlier this month it was also named for the first time as one of the best big companies to work for in the Sunday Times annual survey.

A full list of stores and advice for customers on owning a pet can be found at www.jollyes.co.uk. 

Don’t worry if you don’t have a store nearby, you can shop and find helpful advice on our website.
title: Fussy husky, amazing good
review: I have a very fussy husky and I was recommended a dog food from Jollyes in Cadbury Garden Centre from a friend,  and I wanted to check if I tried a dog food and my dog didn’t like it that I was able to return it, the helpful assistant said I could. The food I was also looking to purchase (lifestage) she advised was popular and not many people bring it back. Lo and behold it’s work and my dog loves it! I will be returning to purchase more and thanks to her for asking if I am a member, she signed me and now I get a little discount so thank you :)

However, I gave three stars because I feel there’s room for improvement, especially when it comes to options for cats.It’s great that you’ve added refrigerators for fresh meat, but why are there only options for dogs? Cats deserve the same level of variety and quality, but right now, their choices are quite limited compared to dogs. I hope to see more cat-friendly products in the future because otherwise, this store is fantastic!
